title: runIT library part
description: A physical thing of the hardware canvas (library/parts/<id>/part.json): a board, a module (a devkit / breakout), a chip, an actuator, a sensor or a passive part. Its drawing is part.svg beside it, in millimetres. Its connectors are standard components (goldpin headers, screw terminals, wire leads...) placed on it; each pin says what it is: ground, a power net of the part, a pin of a device, a config pin of the part's own device, a bus line, an H-bridge output or a motor lead. The power section is the part's own flow of energy (sources, fuses, regulators, muxes, loads) between its nets. LIBRARY.md describes it.

id.description: The part's id: the name of its folder.

name.description: What the palette and the canvas call it.

category.description: The palette's group. A board is what the project's devices sit on; a module carries a device of its own (a PCA9685 breakout); a chip is a bare IC or module for the PCB creator.

board.description: A board part: the board.json it draws (name and revision): the canvas shows it for a project on that board.

graphic.description: The drawing beside part.json (part.svg), viewBox in mm (0 0 w h). Connectors are not in it: the app draws them from 'connectors', at their true size.

device.description: The device the part is: placing it on the canvas adds a project device of this type, with the preset's values and then 'config'.

config.description: Config values by field id, over the preset's.

nets.description: The part's power nets. A pin with 'net' is on one; its role says whether the part takes power there, gives it, or only passes it on (a breakout's V+ that runs to its servo headers).

power.description: How energy flows inside the part (a board): elements between its nets.

chips.description: Generic chips drawn on a board (the PCB creator): a labelled rectangle, optionally a device of the board.

type.description: A device descriptor's id, or a library part's id (esp32s3_wroom1).

device.description: The board device it is (board.json id).

role.description: sink: the part takes power here (a servo's VCC); source: the part gives it (a board's rail, driven by an element of 'power'); through: it only passes power between its pins (a breakout's V+); internal: a board net no pin reaches.

voltage_mV.description: A sink: what it accepts (nominal: what it wants). A source: what it can give.

max_mA.description: A source or through net: the most it carries.

monitor.description: A power monitor channel that measures this net.

pin.description: One pin of a connector. At most one of gnd / net / device_pin / config / bus / hbridge / motor / nc says what it is.

at.description: A pad connector only: where the pin is, in the part's mm.

net.description: A power net of the part ('nets').

device_pin.description: A pin of a device that something can use: a board device by its id, or the part's own device ('self').

config.description: A pin-reference config field of the part's own device: the pin this one is wired to goes there (a servo's pwm_pin).

bus.description: A board's bus number (board.json i2c_buses). A part that needs a bus leaves it out: its device's bus follows the wire.

hbridge.description: An H-bridge output (OUT1 = channel 0); 'supply' is the net that powers it.

motor.description: A lead of a motor: the two go to the two outputs of one bridge. Its draw is the part's 'motor' net (role sink).

type.description: A standard component: the app draws it at its true size (goldpins 2.54 mm).

at.description: The centre of its first pin, in the part's mm (a wire: where its plug is).

pitch_mm.description: Screw terminal only: 3.5, 5.0 or 5.08 (goldpins are always 2.54).

rows.description: Goldpin: rows of pins (pins are listed row by row).

from.description: A wire: where it leaves the part.

kind.description: source: energy enters (USB PD, an input); fuse: an eFuse between two nets; regulator: makes 'out' from 'in'; mux: 'out' from one of 'in'; load: what the part itself draws from 'in'.

device.description: The board device that is it (a regulator's VOLTAGE, a mux's SOURCE, a USB PD sink).

voltage_mV.description: A source or regulator: what it can give.

adjustable.description: A regulator the board sets (POWER_VREG VOLTAGE): the canvas sets it for what is connected.

levels_mV.description: A source that gives only these voltages (the fixed levels of USB PD).

inputs.description: A mux: the name of each input, in the order of 'in' (the POWER_SUPPLY SOURCE value).
